hypothesis: Dropping the repeated table-section clean in a733_cached_prepare removes 321 (diagnostic) or 449 (supervised) DC CVAC operations per boot with every other maintenance count unchanged.
prediction: Budgets against baseline commit 0fd1b51 (images built from it, host checks named per row). Table-section DC CVAC in a733_cached_prepare(): 321 lines (diagnostic), 449 (supervised), one publish call -> 0 lines and no call naming __tables_start (checks/cpu-table-walks.py, from the disassembly of a733_cached_prepare()). Table-line maintenance per boot, eight-core diagnostic image (derived): 1,666 (321 + 321 + 8 x 128) -> 1,345. Supervised image (derived): 2,178 (449 + 449 + 128 + 128 + 8 x 128) -> 1,729, adding the two 128-line step 3 terms from checks/a733-supervised-publication.py. Lines that a733_supervised_ns_publish() maintains: 42,172 -> 42,172 (maintained_lines). EL1 table DC CIVAC per core before SCTLR_EL1.M: 128 -> 128. Pool translations 392 AT and the golden EL1 map unchanged (checks/device-memory-capacity.py). Operation 5 response on the device: 1,160 bytes in 1 tick, unchanged (checks/usb0-service-burst.py). Time saved is an estimate, no source is pinned for the cost of one maintenance operation: at 494 MHz and an assumed 70 cycles per operation, 321 removed operations save about 0.05 ms per boot (diagnostic) and 449 about 0.06 ms (supervised). QEMU and the Unicorn models do not model caches. Reasoning for removing step 2: the table section holds the five EL3 and EL1 pages and the checksum line, 321 lines of 64 bytes in the diagnostic image and 449 in the supervised image, whose section also holds the two temporary EL3 pages of platform/a733-smp-supervised/publication.S. Step 1 (a733_cached_memory_prepare in memory.c) runs DC CIVAC over the section, DSB SY, then writes every descriptor and the checksum. Step 2 (continue.c DC CVAC through a733_cpu_coherence_publish) acts only on lines present when it runs; between step 1 and step 2 core 0 is the only running core, no DMA master is admitted and SCTLR_EL3 M, C, I are clear (a733_cached_memory_prepare refuses to run otherwise), so every data access is Device-nGnRnE and allocates no line, and the only other maintenance is the DC CVAC publication of code and initial RAM, which allocates nothing. Each eight-core boot is evidence that the rule holds: prepare_core(0) writes a733_cached_records after the publications with no maintenance and each secondary reads those records at EL3 with the MMU off; stale records would stop the boot at the record barrier's deadline. Step 3 (supervised only: a733_supervised_ns_publish cleans the two temporary EL3 pages, enables EL3 translation with SCTLR_EL3.C clear through a temporary map making the Non-secure alias of DRAM Normal non-cacheable, and runs DC IVAC over image RAM and the EL1 root and level-2 pages, 64 lines each) stays, and step 4 (each core at EL1 with the MMU off runs DC CIVAC over the EL1 root and level-2 pages in a733_cpu_coherence_enable_el1(), reads both pages back with Device loads and compares their sum with the recorded checksum before setting SCTLR_EL1.M) stays. Covering checks for step 2: checks/cpu-table-walks.py (the flush is called before the table builder, every flushed line precedes the first table-section write, enable_el1 issues 128 DC CIVAC and 512 LDP in the linked image) and checks/a733-cpu-coherence.py (enable_el1 flushes both EL1 pages before any system-register write; a wrong checksum or a malformed root entry 1 leaves SCTLR_EL1.M clear).

conditions.base: commit 8e40a70, the integration commit this change starts from, exported with git archive into its own directory (budget baseline images from commit 0fd1b51)
conditions.head: the commit that adds the design, with the edits outside its owned files applied: the measurement in checks/cpu-table-walks.py, the three capacity fixtures, the launcher flag and its check, the comment in platform/a733/cpu_coherence.S and the two component documents
conditions.images: every central target linking platform/a733-smp-cached/continue.c: cached diagnostic, observer and supervised eight-core images, and the board, camera, GPU render, HDMI, mimus native, cached-devices and storage-maintenance images; the supervised image alone links platform/a733-smp-supervised/publication.S; also the integrated OS image in resident and supervised lifetimes and the QEMU kernel check and eight-core soak images; Clang 21.1.8 and ld.lld
conditions.tools: checks/cpu-table-walks.py from the head tree with --baseline on base images (runs a733_cached_prepare() from the linked image in Unicorn with callees stubbed and records the range of each a733_cpu_coherence_publish() call); checks/device-memory-capacity.py from each tree on that tree's fixtures, executed by QEMU 10.2.1

conclusion: Every budget is met. The table-section publication is gone from a733_cached_prepare() in every image: a disassembly scan finds three publish calls and one address load of the table page in each of the eleven base images and two calls and no table-page load in each head image. The two remaining publish calls are code at 0x41000000 (2 MiB) and initial RAM from 0x41200000 to __bss_end. Per-boot totals: base 321 + 321 + 8 x 128 = 1,666 and 449 + 449 + 128 + 128 + 8 x 128 = 2,178; head 321 + 8 x 128 = 1,345 and 449 + 128 + 128 + 8 x 128 = 1,729 (the supervised image adds the 128-line DC CVAC of its two temporary EL3 pages and the 128-line Non-secure DC IVAC of the EL1 pages in publication.S). a733_cached_prepare() shrinks by 36 bytes (the third publish call and its arguments, 9 instructions); .text of every rebuilt image is unchanged because the 36 bytes fall inside existing alignment padding. checks/cpu-table-walks.py cannot model the camera, GPU render, mimus native and cached-devices images (two repeat a structure name with different layouts across compilation units, two use the extended device-memory profile its preparation model does not cover); the disassembly scan covers those four. The capacity fixtures no longer publish the table section so their code and data move: builder functions disassemble to the same instructions apart from addresses, and three QEMU-trace instruction counts moved by -5 to +10 (builder with the decode check passing 20,785 -> 20,795, builder of the read-only-view fixture with the check failing 15,668 -> 15,663, local pool preparation of the uncached fixture 987 -> 984). AT, DC, TLBI, DSB, DMB and ISB counts in every traced case are unchanged, as are the exact PMU count of the publication run (22,541 instructions), the 392 translations, the EL1 map size and all 13 native cases. No figure describes physical cache or coherence behaviour. Unproven (Arm Architecture Reference Manual, not pinned): that EL3 and EL1 with the MMU off address the Secure and the Non-secure space, that Device accesses allocate no cache line, and that maintenance issued with the MMU off reaches every core; removing step 2 makes the tables depend on the second rule.
narrative: Checks run on the head: checks/cpu-table-walks.py on the diagnostic image pass, 8 cases including the new publication case; checks/a733-cpu-coherence.py pass, 41 native and reference cases; checks/a733-supervised-publication.py default and --all-core-transition-only pass, all eight modeled cores reach cached EL1; checks/a733-smp-cached.py on the diagnostic image pass, eight-core scheduler and missing-secondary refusal; checks/device-memory-capacity.py pass, 13 native cases; checks/cached-device-reservations.py pass, eight cores; checks/usb0-service-burst.py pass (operation 5 response 1 tick, 3 packets, base and head); tools/check-kernel.py pass; tools/check-smp.py --case soak8 pass, one trial. Why step 3 stays: it is the only Non-secure maintenance that core 0 runs on its own caches before it releases the secondaries; core 0's step 4 is not ordered before any secondary's step 4 or before that secondary sets SCTLR_EL1.M; no pinned source shows that maintenance issued with the MMU off is broadcast to other cores; without step 3 a Non-secure dirty line left in core 0's caches by the boot loader could be written back after a secondary's checksum passed and that secondary would walk corrupted tables undetected. The .Lel1_root and .Lel1_l2 loops can go once a pinned source proves MMU-off maintenance is broadcast, or once the Non-secure dirty-line experiment of docs/cold-entry.md passes on every launch path. Left out: the DC CVAC of the two temporary EL3 pages in publication.S (128 lines), because the dirty-line experiment of docs/cold-entry.md uses that temporary mapping; a supervised per-core flush assertion in checks/a733-supervised-publication.py, which covers no case that checks/cpu-table-walks.py and checks/a733-cpu-coherence.py miss; a host command that opens the board itself; changes to usb0.c or the report layout. DC IVAC cleaning a dirty line on the Cortex-A55: TRM 100442_0200_00 section A6.2.4, pinned as recorded in docs/designs/cpu-table-walks.md. The change adds no hardware register sequence. continue.S is unchanged, so the continue.S hash pins in cmake/a733-smp-observe.cmake and cmake/a733-storage-maintenance.cmake stay; no pin covers continue.c. Interrupts, memory placement and synchronization are unchanged: step 2 ran on core 0 with exceptions masked before any secondary release.

hypothesis: The host reader fetch() in tools/fault-report.py obtains the 1,160-byte operation 5 report in one request with one copy per byte and refuses every malformed exchange.
prediction: One request, at most 3 reads with 512-byte fragments, 0 retries; one copy per report byte on the host (fragments appended to one buffer). Host rows measured by checks/fault-report.py against a modeled device that applies the operation 5 rules of usb0.c and returns no more than each read requests, in fragments of 1, 29 and 512 bytes.

conditions.kind: host model; no image, device or USB library
conditions.check: checks/fault-report.py; checks/os-image-launch.py on the supervised OS image (21 cases, four for --fault-report)

conclusion: With 512-byte fragments fetch() reads 512, 512 and 136 bytes in three reads, requesting 1,536, 1,024 and 512 bytes; the read count follows the device's fragment size. Fragments are appended to one bytearray, and retain() and the caller receive the same read-only view. checks/fault-report.py passes 15 cases. Altered copies of tools/fault-report.py fail the check: without the size limit, the empty-fragment test, the read rounding, any one of the identity checks, the final deadline test, or the single buffer. Operation 5 response on the device is unchanged at 1,160 bytes in 1 tick, 3 packets, since the device side is unchanged.
narrative: Cases: a non-empty 1,160-byte report returned byte for byte after one retain() call with the same bytes; the request bytes compared with FAULT_OP and the zero-field rule parsed from usb0.c and the response size compared with REPORT_BYTES in the decoder; refusals for a device that stops without answering (one write, no retry), an extra byte in the transfer that completes the report, an empty fragment, an identity change before each transfer and before retain(), and a deadline that expires before the write, during the reads and after the last read; an extra byte that arrives in a later transfer stays on endpoint 0x81, so the first response of the capture exchange that follows begins with it and the frame checks of that exchange refuse the shifted frame; a static check of the syntax tree (no usb, usb1, libusb, serial or subprocess import, no /dev/bus/usb or usb-access text, no __main__ block or argument parser). Design of fetch(): writes the 16-byte request struct.pack('<BBHIQ', 5, 0, 0, 0, 0) to endpoint 0x02 once, reads endpoint 0x81 with each read requesting the remaining length rounded up to a multiple of 512 bytes until it holds 1,160 bytes, calls same() before every transfer, caps each transfer's timeout at 500 ms and at least 1 ms of the time left before the deadline. It was derived from device_exchange() (now in tools/sunstone-perf.py). Device interrupts and polling: the shared USB0 loop services once per 1 ms tick; on the host each read blocks in the USB stack. The report is immutable after core 0 builds it, so the USB0 task reads it without a lock or cache maintenance. The report is made visible to EL1 by the DC CVAC of 0x41200000 to __bss_end in continue.c and, in the supervised image, the image-RAM DC IVAC loop of publication.S.

hypothesis: The rebuilt images boot on all eight cores without the table publication, and fetch() returns the slots of a deliberate fault after a WDT0 reset.
prediction: Supervised and diagnostic boot: each rebuilt image reaches the scheduler on all eight cores with no stop 0x102, 0x108 or EL1 table-check refusal. Report after reset: after a WDT0 reset, fetch() returns a report whose slots match the deliberate fault (item 3 of the board evidence of docs/fault-capture.md).
conclusion: Not yet run on the board; no figure of cpu-leftovers has been measured there.
narrative: Open board runs listed under the open work of docs/designs/cpu-leftovers.md.
